# Aspen paper audit — independent review

The reviewer did not author the supplied draft. Main source SHA-256: 8dc6f207a0b8fc8abe4b12849e335d583df34231b8f4e9e66dd8f8ec8a78eb5e. Bibliography SHA-256: dbd312eced6c7ee98e29e916d68651bbbfeac92cb58fd80bdb22fbb296375d84. Sources are unchanged.

332 OK / 15 FIX across 347 claim, caption, equation and table-cell rows. The structured audit is receipts/acd_stage5b_paper_audit.json. Each row preserves the original TeX claim and semantic receipt or code sources. Numeric values are retained at full precision; display and percentage conversion are stated. Qualitative and definitional claims use the cited contract or code.

Todd-licensed deviations, not FIX: title, opening framing sentence, defined forecast-sign shorthand, and the labelled exploratory development amplitude sentence. These rulings do not supply a new formal route at changed amplitudes or a mechanism license outside L1–L10 for headline assembly.
Full_precision uses curated semantic quantities and actual registry/receipt/contract sources. No generic rounding-candidate selection or unrelated percentage conversion is used. Where several claims share a paragraph, the named values form that paragraph’s scientific context; table cells retain their individual exact sources.

R-other: the corrected L9 U denominator is all S questions in the answered lead range. At changed amplitudes the formal order status is PREREQUISITE NOT MET; zero-crossing intervals are numerical exploratory results. No posterior, MAP, RML, integration, inference, training, cloud access or TeX build occurred during review.

Methods checked against frozen WO sections 3–14 and scientific/code freezes: Lorenz-96 equation; RK4, timestep and double precision; inherited RMS normalization; spin-up and all-site Gaussian observations; action patterns, cost and windows; question definitions and ties; priors and likelihood; fit starts and omitted fitting prior; NUTS, four chains and thinning; parameter and functional diagnostics; all-draw fallback, retries and exclusions; Gaussian, joint-adjoint and timestep checks; null and modal climate confidence; seed disjointness and confirmation blind order; case unit, count floors, betting/Clopper–Pearson/McNemar statistics and cut order; crude/RML constructions; CNN checkpoint provenance, window encoding and shared member validity; targeting population, linear-Gaussian greedy selector, probes and common refit denominator; figures and aggregation scopes.

R1m stored bootstrap intervals are approximate and descriptive. The figure bands are interquartile dispersion, not bootstrap uncertainty. Ratios of medians are distinct from medians of ratios. Window divergence is the median of per-case/action window averages. Bibliography fields are metadata; primary texts were not fetched. Literature context is checked against saved WO summaries where present, with unsupported assertions flagged.

## Open FIX rows

- P033_05 (line 33): Present this as the paper’s question: “We ask whether an intervention-sign confidence horizon matches the confidence horizon of the sign of the unforced window-energy anomaly.”
- P037_05 (line 37): “The protocol and development reading were frozen before confirmation observations and outcomes were generated.”
- P043_01 (line 43): Move this descriptive z-ratio interpretation to Results or Discussion. In the introduction retain the L4 median correlation and cancellation values.
- P043_02 (line 43): Replace the ordering claim with exploratory loss-difference point estimates −0.228, −0.220 and −0.210 at amplitudes 0.04, 0.08 and 0.16. State that calibration at changed amplitudes was not recomputed and their formal R2b prerequisites are unmet. At 0.32 and 0.64 the numerical intervals span zero. Move the linear-response hypothesis to Discussion.
- P094_03 (line 94): “Confident forecast-sign answers pass the separate R0-F criterion at every evaluable lead: at least 30 confident cases and an exact one-sided 95% lower bound of at least 0.90.”
- P118_02 (line 118): Give the observed shares without equivalence wording: “At 0 LT the shares are 98.3% and 97.0%; at 1 LT they are 91.4% and 92.0%.”
- P118_03 (line 118): Label the per-lead all-confidence shares descriptive. State the formal DIFFERS result using observation-confident S and confident Fc at 2 and 3 LT only.
- P118_06 (line 118): “For the other seven patterns the climatological modal sign has probability 0.50–0.56 at every lead, so neither sign is climate-confident.”
- P166_06 (line 166): “The exploratory loss-difference intervals span zero at amplitudes 0.32 and 0.64; their formal R2b status is PREREQUISITE NOT MET.”
- P196_01 (line 196): “We use a 128-member ensemble formed by perturbing the last observed frame with observation noise and using the forcing estimated from the observations.”
- P205_01 (line 205): Add: “Posterior, crude and development RML aggregate all 38 saved question types at all eight leads, including P/B at leads omitted from the confidence maps; CNN uses 2 LT only. Curves are descriptive and do not establish an ordering.”
- P210_09 (line 210): Add the frozen requirements: Q must settle at least 20 answers, its exact one-sided 95% accuracy lower bound must be at least 0.80, and its post-probe truth coverage must be at least 0.85. State that confirmation Q settled 15 of 60, below the 20-answer floor, as well as failing the margin and paired-test requirements.
- P231_03 (line 231): “The observed displacement-to-spread ratio is roughly stable after 1 LT, consistent with shared growth of displacement and spread; the mechanism was not identified.”
- P233_04 (line 233): “Under the linear-response approximation a positive amplitude scales mean and spread together. The three smallest tested development amplitudes have similar confident shares; realized calibration at changed amplitudes was not recomputed.”
- P247_02 (line 247): “At 0 LT the observed confidence shares are 98.3% and 97.0%. The calibrated observation-confident S/Fc comparison differs at 2 and 3 LT, and the paired loss reading is PRECEDES.”

### Open findings retained

- **P033_05 (line 33), declined, pending Todd.** Implicit in both is that a decision made from a forecast can be trusted about as far ahead as the forecast it is made from. Proposed fix: Present this as the paper’s question: “We ask whether an intervention-sign confidence horizon matches the confidence horizon of the sign of the unforced window-energy anomaly.”
- **P043_01 (line 43), declined, pending Todd.** \item The shared uncertainty makes the intervention's effect much sharper than the forecast anomaly just after the observation window, but that advantage decays faster than the forecast's own signal. Proposed fix: Move this descriptive z-ratio interpretation to Results or Discussion. In the introduction retain the L4 median correlation and cancellation values.

Resolution record: R-other retains the two unresolved findings and supplies no additional license. Changed-amplitude zero-crossing intervals are numerical exploratory statements; formal prerequisites remain unmet. The linear-response Discussion is interpreted conditionally under its now-explicit approximation and final no-calibration caveat, not as a calibrated universal result.

Scope resolution: §10 names a settled-count metric, but §11 explicitly bans the word settled. R-other therefore uses confident/resolved counts. Ordinary fixed experimental-design language is not a claim of deterministic certainty, and negative statements denying a guarantee remain appropriate qualifications.
